decisions.decision: Declined to add any ESLint plugin enforcing "use client" directive presence. Checked 4 npm candidates via this project's package-legitimacy tool: 3 were SUS (low weekly downloads, or high downloads with no public repo), the 1 OK-verdict package (eslint-plugin-react-server-components) is a single-maintainer, 41-star, single-rule plugin. Decided the existing Next.js compiler build-time error (which already hard-fails with a specific message when a Server Component uses a client-only API) is sufficient; a lint rule would only add editor-time speed, not close a real silent-failure gap.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with this project's established bar for adding dependencies (same caution applied to the 01-18 gitleaks-wrapper rejection) — no candidate cleared that bar for the marginal benefit offered.

decisions.decision: Declined to add any "use server" directive lint enforcement.
decisions.rationale: No plugin exists for this at all (searched), and moot regardless — this project has zero Server Actions anywhere (ADR tech/0002 chose Route Handlers + TanStack Query over Server Actions), so there is nothing for such a rule to ever apply to today.
